newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds narrowly mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds narrowly mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Brady bond prices were narrowly mixed in light trade on Thursday and market experts said activity was expected to remain that way until the first week of June when a slew of U.S. economic reports were to be released.

"It's pretty boring today. No one is going to be able to make a hard and fast comment about the decision of the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) until they see the next set of U.S. data and there is no meaningful data until the first week of June," said one trader at a U.S. investment bank in London.

Brazilian Brady debt posted slim gains following late news from Brasilia on Wednesday that the country's Senate approved a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term. The bill has already been approved by the lower house of Congress but must still pass a second vote in the senate in order to become law.
"Prices were up on the back of Brazilian senate passing a re-election amendment for Cardoso," said one trader.
Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/8 firmer at 78-3/4 bid after rising 1-3/8 in New York on Wednesday on news that the country unveiled an offer to swap or buy back Brady debt.

On Wednesday, Brazil announced an offer to either repurchase outright par bonds and discount Z-L bonds or to swap pars, discounts, or "C" bonds for up to $1.0 billion of 30-year uncollateralized global bonds. The offer will expire on June 3 at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT unless extended or ended earlier by Brazil.
Meanwhile, market experts said emerging market debt should outperform the U.S. Treasury market given the absence of fresh U.S. economic data.

"I think the emerging markets as an asset group will outperform the U.S. Treasury market fairly substantially. I think people will look for yield and, with this vaccuum for the next 10 days, there is no reason not to be invested," said one Brady bond trader.
"Provided you have a hedge in place with U.S. Treasuries, why wouldn't you want to be long emerging market debt," he added.
Among Eastern European debt instruments, Bulgaria IABs were unchanged at 67-1/8 bid and Russian dollar-Vnesheconombank loans were 1/4 weaker at 85-3/4 bid.
